info.title: Turnstile Liquidity Analyst
info.summary: Is this Uniswap v3 pool safe to LP? Answered from indexed history and a live quote, not from TVL.
info.description:
Turnstile sells a **judgement**, not a query result.

The one question it answers is: *is this pool safe to provide liquidity to?* That is not the same as "what is its TVL", and the difference is the product. An LP is short volatility and long fees, exposed to the pool's inventory rather than to its headline number, so the analyst combines two sources that disagree in useful ways:

| Source | Answers | Cannot answer |
|---|---|---|
| A Messari-conformant DEX AMM subgraph on The Graph | what the pool *has been* — realized fee revenue, trading continuity, LP count, age | it is indexed, therefore behind; its USD prices are derived from pools, so checking a pool against them is circular |
| Uniswap **QuoterV2**, at the current block | what the pool *will do* — depth at size, slippage, initialized ticks crossed | one instant, with no history and no notion of whether that instant is typical |

Neither source alone answers the question. Cumulative volume cannot tell you the pool emptied yesterday; a live quote cannot tell you it only ever trades for one hour a day. The verdict exists in the gap between them.

**Every response states its own provenance and its own caveats.** `confidence` is not decoration: it falls when there is no live quote, when the subgraph is stale, when a token is unpriced, and when the depth ladder had to be sized using a price the subgraph derived from the very pool under examination. A response never silently omits what it could not get — read `caveats` before acting on `rating`.

**Payment.** Both `/analyze` routes are x402-protected and answer `402 Payment Required` with a signed challenge before they answer anything else. Settlement is real: Turnstile settles on Hedera testnet through the Blocky402 facilitator and writes a receipt to an HCS topic, retrievable afterwards from `/receipts/{transaction}`. The unpaid request is never charged for work that could not have succeeded — a malformed pool address is rejected with `400` before a challenge is issued.

get.summary: LP-safety verdict from indexed history alone ($0.07).
get.description:
**When to use this.** You are screening — ranking or filtering many pools, and you want something better than a TVL sort without paying for a live quote on every candidate. This is the cheap pass.

**What it does.** Answers from the Messari-conformant subgraph on The Graph only: realized fee revenue, trading continuity across sparse hourly buckets, pool age, LP count, and the two-sidedness of reserves. It costs one indexed query and no RPC call, which is most of why it is cheaper.

**What it cannot tell you, and says so.** There is no live quote in this tier, so it cannot tell you what a trade would actually execute at right now. The verdict states this in `caveats` and carries a lower `confidence` accordingly — it reports that it is flying blind rather than pretending otherwise. A pool can look healthy across its whole indexed history and still be unable to fill a $1,000 trade at this instant; only `analyzePoolAttested` can see that.

**How to read the result.** `rating` is the answer; `signals[]` is why. A `structural` signal that fails means the pool is not a venue at all and one is enough to justify AVOID. A non-structural failure is a reason for care, not for walking away. Each signal carries the numbers its headline rests on, so the conclusion is auditable rather than asserted.

**Cost.** $0.07 per call. Escalate to `analyzePoolAttested` for the candidates that survive this pass.

200.description: The verdict, with the tier that produced it.

get.summary: LP-safety verdict with a live Uniswap depth ladder and the re-derivable scorer input ($0.35).
get.description:
**When to use this.** You are about to commit capital, or you need a number you can defend to someone else. Use it on the shortlist that `analyzePoolStandard` produced, not on every candidate.

**Why it costs five times as much.** It adds the half of the evidence that history cannot supply. Alongside the same subgraph history, it quotes the pool **live against Uniswap QuoterV2 at the current block**, walking a depth ladder — typically $1k, $10k, $100k, $1M, $10M — and reporting for each rung the executed output, the realized slippage, and the number of **initialized ticks crossed**. Ticks crossed is the load-bearing number: in concentrated liquidity it tells you how much of the range the trade had to eat through, which is what actually determines whether the next trade is worse.

**The finding this tier exists to produce.** Combining the two sources yields conclusions neither can reach alone. On Uniswap v3 USDC/WETH 0.05% the verdict is ACCEPTABLE at 75% confidence — and the live ladder shows that only **0.944%** of the pool's claimed TVL is reachable within 1% slippage. The subgraph supplies the claimed TVL; the quoter supplies the reachable depth; the ratio is the answer, and it exists only because both were asked. In concentrated liquidity a small ratio is normal, since most capital sits outside the active range by design — but it does mean the headline number overstates fee-earning capital by two orders of magnitude, and an LP sizing a position off TVL will be disappointed.

**Where the two sources disagree, believe the quote.** The subgraph is indexed and therefore behind; `provenance.subgraphLagSeconds` tells you by how much. The quote is taken at `provenance.depthBlock` and is the only measurement here that reflects the pool as it is now.

**What else you get.** The complete `analystInput` — about 9KB of plain JSON — which is the exact argument the scorer was called with. The scorer is a pure total function of it, so a buyer holding this object can re-derive the verdict independently and get the same bytes. The claim is checkable rather than merely asserted. `attestation` carries the Chainlink TEE attestation over those bytes when one is available, and degrades explicitly rather than silently when it is not.

**Cost.** $0.35 per call, under the $0.50 ceiling published on-chain for this service.

200.description: The verdict, the live depth profile inside it, the scorer input, and the attestation over that input.

analystInput.description: The exact argument the pure scorer was called with. Re-run it to reproduce `verdict` byte for byte.

attestation.description: Attestation over the bytes of `analystInput`. Null or degraded when no attester was reachable — never silently omitted.

get.summary: Look up the settlement receipt for a payment already made. Free.
get.description:
**When to use this.** After paying, to prove you paid — for reconciliation, for an audit trail, or to show a third party that a specific verdict was bought rather than fabricated.

Takes the transaction identifier from the `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header of a paid call and returns the rail's receipt for it. On the Hedera rail this is backed by a message on an HCS consensus topic, so the receipt is independently verifiable on a public ledger rather than only in Turnstile's own records.

Free, and unauthenticated: a receipt is evidence, and evidence you have to pay to see is worth less.

parameters.name: transaction
parameters.description: Rail-specific transaction id, as returned in the `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` header of the paid call. On Hedera this looks like `0.0.7162784@1788791855.758948636`.

200.description: The receipt, as the settling rail recorded it.

404.description: No rail holds a receipt for that transaction.

get.summary: Service state, live payment rails, and current tier pricing. Free.
get.description:
**When to use this.** Before the first paid call in a session — to learn the current price of each tier rather than assuming one, and to check `settlementLive` before relying on a payment actually moving value.

`settlementLive` is deliberately honest: it is `false` when every advertised rail is still a placeholder. A demo that quietly settles nothing is worse than one that says so.

Free and unauthenticated.

200.description: Service name, whether any rail settles real value, the rails, and the tiers with their prices in USD.

settlementLive.description: True when at least one advertised rail settles real value. False when every rail is a placeholder.

Pool.name: pool
Pool.description: The Uniswap v3 pool contract address, checksummed or lowercase. Must be a pool the subgraph has indexed.

usdcWeth005.summary: Uniswap v3 USDC/WETH 0.05% — the worked example in this spec's descriptions

BadPool.description: The path parameter is not a pool address. Raised **before** a payment challenge is issued, so a payer is never charged for a request that could not have succeeded.

PaymentRequired.description: x402 v2 payment challenge. The same `PaymentRequired` object appears base64-encoded in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` response header and as the JSON body — the header is what the protocol reads, the body is what a human with curl sees. Retry the request with the signed payload in `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`; the paid `200` carries the settlement in `PAYMENT-RESPONSE`.

PAYMENT-REQUIRED.description: base64 of the `PaymentRequired` object. x402 **v2** — not v1's `X-PAYMENT`.

accepts.description: One entry per rail willing to settle this request. Pick one.

amount.description: In the asset's smallest unit, as a string.

ServiceError.description: The service could not complete the analysis.

Verdict.description: The answer to "is this pool safe to LP?", with the reasoning that produced it and the provenance needed to judge whether it has aged.

rating.description: `INSUFFICIENT_DATA` is a real answer, not an error. It means the evidence did not support any verdict.

confidence.description: How much of the evidence the analyst wanted was actually available. Falls with no live quote, a stale subgraph, an unpriced token, or a self-referential price.

signals.description: The reasoning, one observation per entry. This is why the rating is what it is.

provenance.description: What a reader needs in order to judge whether this verdict has aged.

subgraph.description: The subgraph endpoint the history came from.

subgraphTransport.description: `mcp` when queried through the Subgraph MCP server, `http` when queried directly.

subgraphLagSeconds.description: Seconds between the subgraph head and the assessment. How far behind the history is.

depthProvider.description: Null on the standard tier — that tier takes no live quote.

depthBlock.description: The chain head the live quote was taken at. This is the number that makes a verdict current.

caveats.description: Everything the analyst wanted and did not get. Never silently empty — read this before acting on `rating`.

Signal.description: One reasoned observation. The evidence is what makes the verdict auditable rather than asserted.

structural.description: A structural signal describes whether the pool is a *venue* at all. One failing structural signal is enough to justify AVOID; a non-structural one is a reason for care, not for walking away.

headline.description: One sentence: the conclusion and the number it rests on.

evidence.description: The labelled numbers the headline is derived from.

reasoning.description: Why that evidence implies that verdict, for an LP specifically.

AnalystInput.description: The complete, serializable argument to the pure scorer. Premium tier only. Nothing in it is a handle, and `now` is a field rather than a clock read, which is what makes the verdict reproducible.

depth.description: Null when live depth could not be obtained. The verdict must then say so in `caveats`.

now.description: Unix seconds, supplied rather than read, so scoring stays deterministic.

PoolFacts.description: Everything the scorer knows about a pool's history. Sourced from the subgraph.

createdTimestamp.description: Unix seconds the pool was created on chain — the honest floor for "how long has this existed".

totalValueLockedUSD.description: The *claimed* TVL. Compare it against the depth ladder before trusting it.

cumulativeSupplySideRevenueUSD.description: Realized LP revenue. Realized, not projected.

feeTierPct.description: The LP-facing trading fee as a percentage — 0.05 means 0.05%.

tick.description: Null on a non-concentrated AMM or an uninitialized pool.

hourly.description: Closed hourly intervals, most recent first. **Sparse**: an hour with no activity produces no row at all rather than a row of zeroes, so activity must be measured against elapsed hours and not against the row count.

source.description: Where the history came from, so a verdict can name its source.

blockTimestamp.description: Unix seconds of the subgraph's head block — not of the query.

TokenFacts.description: One side of a pool, as the subgraph reports it.

priceUSD.description: Subgraph-derived. Null when the subgraph could not anchor it — and note it is derived from pools, so checking a pool against it is circular.

balance.description: Pool reserve in whole tokens, already decimal-adjusted.

HourlyBucket.description: One closed hourly interval from a Messari `LiquidityPoolHourlySnapshot`.

hour.description: `floor(unixSeconds / 3600)` — the interval's identity, carried so sparse buckets can be counted against elapsed hours.

timestamp.description: Unix seconds of the block that closed the interval. Not an hour boundary.

DepthProfile.description: Live depth-at-size from Uniswap. The half of the evidence that history cannot supply.

providerDetail.description: Human-readable provenance — the QuoterV2 address and the RPC host.

atBlock.description: Chain head at quote time. The number that makes this live.

quotedAt.description: Unix seconds when the quotes were taken.

rungs.description: The depth ladder, ascending by notional.

notionalPricing.description: How the USD notionals were converted into token amounts.

priceSource.description: The scorer downgrades confidence on a self-referential price — one derived from the pool being examined.

DepthRung.description: One rung of the depth ladder: what a trade of this size actually gets.

notionalUSD.description: The notional this rung was sized at, in USD.

amountOut.description: Output in whole tokens. Null when the quote reverted.

executedRate.description: `amountOut / amountIn`. Null when the quote reverted.

ticksCrossed.description: Initialized ticks the swap crossed. In concentrated liquidity this is how much of the range the trade had to eat through, and therefore how much worse the next trade will be. Null when the provider does not report it.

error.description: Present only on a failed rung — the revert or API error, verbatim.
